lines.text: Light travels in straight lines, until it enters glass.
lines.visual: Ink plate: five parallel rays cross from the left and meet the hairline outline of a convex lens.

lines.text: Glass slows it down, so every ray bends toward the thick middle, and they all cross at one point: the focus.
lines.visual: The rays refract at the lens and converge; the focal point is the one glowing thing (signal layer).

lines.text: Move the object closer, and its image moves away.
lines.visual: Bone paper, inside the Shorts square: an object arrow slides toward the lens and its inverted image slides out.

short.hook_title: Why a lens has one focus

lines.text: One short equation predicts exactly where the image lands.
lines.visual: manim-web layer: the thin-lens equation is written in, 1/f = 1/d_o + 1/d_i.

short.hook_title: Why a lens has one focus
